00 Context

Why now, and the box the design has to fit inside

CMMC Level 2
NIST 800-171 in scope
~140 staff | ~40 remote
CONSTRAINT 01

Self-hosted control plane

No cloud-hosted management server. Summit must own and operate the plane that authenticates users and distributes policy.

CONSTRAINT 02

Per-user audit trail

Who connected, when, and what they accessed, traceable to a named individual, not a shared VPN pool address.

CONSTRAINT 03

AD + Duo identity

Production access must run through the existing on-prem Active Directory and Duo MFA already in use today.

The trigger Fortinet is sunsetting SSL VPN in FortiOS. The vendor's path (FortiClient EMS + ZTNA) means new licences and infrastructure. Summit wants a self-hosted alternative it controls, and Justin has already proven a NetBird PoC reaches the 10.120.x.x network.

03 Phase 1 | how the four pieces fit

Identity, access, placement, audit

Detail behind the diagram
one panel per decision

A Identity: the critical path

AD + Duo-> IdP (OIDC)-> NetBird

AD speaks LDAP/Kerberos; NetBird speaks OIDC. A federation layer, ADFS (shortest path if Windows licensing exists) or Keycloak, bridges them and keeps Duo MFA at login.

Net-new infrastructure, introduced in parallel.

B Access: least privilege by default

Network> Resources<- Policies

Use NetBird Networks, not flat routes. Resources are defined per service (ERP, file, wiki), reachable only when an AD-group policy says so. Nothing is reachable by default.

"Who can reach the ERP server?" becomes one legible answer.

C Placement: two zones, on purpose

nb-mgmt -> DMZ nb-rp -> Server VLAN

The management plane terminates public connections -> it belongs in a screened subnet (NIST 3.13.5). The routing peer only makes outbound connections -> it sits inside the trust boundary and needs no inbound rules.

"The DMZ host cannot initiate into the Server VLAN."

D Audit: two logs, two jobs

Audit events Traffic events

Control-plane audit events (who changed policy) ship in the OSS build. Per-user traffic events (who reached what, when) satisfy the audit requirement and are an Enterprise feature.

Per-user traffic events are an Enterprise feature.
04 Phase 2 | Operational toil

Four recurring chores: what NetBird ends, and what it honestly doesn't

Scope stated per item
in | partial | out
In scope: NetBird solves it Partial: reduces, not eliminates Out of scope: named honestly

Cloudflare IP allowlists

Mostly out of scope. NetBird won't manage public Cloudflare origin allowlists. But internal users can reach those services over the overlay instead of the public path, removing the need for some public exposure rather than fixing the list.

Reframes the problem | doesn't automate the allowlist

+ Automatic offboarding

AD disable-> SCIM-> access revoked

In scope. SCIM deprovisioning revokes access on AD state; peer login expiration bounds the window for already-connected sessions. SCIM is an Enterprise feature.

Caveat: setup-key peers don't expire, so service identities need their own lifecycle

+ Config backup

PostgreSQL-> nightly dump-> backup server

In scope. Run the management datastore on PostgreSQL (not the default SQLite) so state backs up live, on schedule, the equivalent of today's FortiGate config backup.

The external Postgres datastore is what later enables an HA control plane

+ CI runner access

ephemeral key-> runner peer-> self-cleans

In scope. GitHub Actions runners join with an ephemeral setup key; peers auto-remove after going offline. No standing tunnels to maintain for the dev environment.

Machine identity, governed by key lifecycle, not user login
05 Phase 3 | Site-to-site

Retire the IPsec mesh; routing peers carry the sites

HA routes | metric-based
SCADA stays off the overlay
06 At a glance

The whole migration in three columns

what stays | goes | arrives
across all three phases

Stays

  • FortiGate HA pair, perimeter firewall & segmentation, role narrowed
  • Active Directory + Duo, still the source of identity & MFA
  • Internal DNS, 10.120.1.10 / .11, now reached via routing peer
  • SCADA segmentation, off the overlay, unchanged, throughout
  • Internal 10.0.0.0/8 addressing, no re-IP required

Removed

  • FortiClient SSL VPN, retired after the pilot proves out (P1)
  • IPsec site-to-site tunnels, replaced by routing peers (P3)
  • Manual offboarding in the firewall user list, now AD-driven (P2)
  • Firewall as access-control choke point, policy moves to NetBird
  • Standing CI tunnels, replaced by ephemeral peers (P2)

Added

  • NetBird client on user devices, replacing FortiClient (P1)
  • nb-mgmt, self-hosted control plane in the DMZ (P1)
  • Routing peers, HQ + HA pairs at every site (P1, P3)
  • Identity federation, ADFS/Keycloak bridging AD -> OIDC (P1)
  • Per-user traffic audit + PostgreSQL-backed state (P1, P2)
  • SCIM offboarding & ephemeral CI access (P2)
07 Design decisions

What we recommend, and the one item to validate

recommendations
to walk through together
1

Identity path

Keep AD and Duo and federate to NetBird through an on-prem IdP (ADFS or Keycloak), so access is driven by AD groups and MFA stays where it is today. If a hosted IdP is acceptable, Duo SSO is the simplest option.

sets the
identity
architecture
2

Per-user attribution

Keep masquerade so the FortiGate rules stay untouched, and take per-user audit from NetBird's own traffic events. Attribution lives in the access platform rather than the firewall log. Traffic events are an Enterprise feature.

sets the
audit
model
3

FIPS-validated cryptography (3.13.11)

WireGuard secures every tunnel with modern encryption. Whether a FIPS-validated module is required depends on how the assessor scopes CUI-bearing paths; we validate that early and keep IPsec on any path that must remain FIPS-validated.

validate
with the
assessor
Enterprise features: per-user traffic logging, SCIM provisioning, and an active-active control plane are NetBird Enterprise features. The open-source build runs the rest of the design.
08 End state | the "after"

Everything on one identity-driven overlay, end to end

remote + all sites on NetBird
SSL VPN & IPsec, gone
SCADA still segmented
Summary & execution

One overlay, delivered in parallel.

*One self-hosted, identity-driven overlay replaces SSL VPN and the IPsec mesh, keeps AD, Duo and SCADA segmentation in place, and adds per-user audit, without changing what the FortiGate enforces.
01Phase 1: pilot 5 to 8 remote users in parallel, SSL VPN as fallback, then move all remote users.
02Phase 2: fold in automatic offboarding, scheduled backups, and ephemeral CI access.
03Phase 3: pilot one site, then move site-to-site one at a time, IPsec kept as the per-site fallback.
04Throughout: the FortiGate stays as firewall and rollback path; SCADA stays segmented.
